meta.title: SAM Pro Build Guide
meta.subtitle: Build ServiceNow Software Asset Management Professional on a free Zurich sandbox, one stage at a time.

rules: Only fake data. Never type real names, license keys, contracts or company data into the sandbox.
Never type a password into this guide. It saves what you type in this browser.
The sandbox owner signs in to developer.servicenow.com at least once a week. A sandbox nobody uses for 10 days is deleted.
Tick a step only when you see what **You should see** describes.
End every session with the end-of-session pack. It takes two minutes and keeps the tracker current.

start: Open this guide. On a new computer or browser, load **tracker/progress.json** from the repository (Progress page).
Sign in to the Developer Site and wake the sandbox if it is asleep.
Click **Continue** on the Welcome page. It opens the next step.
during: Follow the steps in order and tick each one when its result matches.
Take the screenshots the steps name and save them with exactly those file names.
Write down what the step asks for in its boxes. These notes go into the tracker.
end: Open **Session report**, fill in who took part and anything that blocked you.
Click **Download end-of-session pack** and unzip it into the repository folder.
Upload the changed files and new screenshots to GitHub.

intro: Companies install software on hundreds of computers. Every program comes with license terms that say how many people, computers or processor cores may use it.
Use more than you bought and the vendor can send a bill after an audit. Buy more than you use and money is wasted. Software Asset Management (SAM) keeps the two in balance.

questions.a: Every program found on every computer, with a clean, standard name.
Every purchase, with the rules of its license.

questions.q: Do they match, and what does it cost?
questions.a: Where we are short (an audit risk), where we pay for unused licenses (waste) and what to do about it.

chain.name: Installation
chain.plain: A scan finds a program on a computer. One record per program per computer.

chain.name: Discovery model
chain.plain: All installations with the same publisher, name and version are grouped into one discovery model.

chain.name: Normalization
chain.plain: Messy names are cleaned into one standard name, such as Microsoft Visio Professional 2021.

chain.name: Software model
chain.plain: The product as we manage it for licensing. It collects the matching installations.

chain.name: Entitlement
chain.plain: What we bought: product, quantity, license metric and price.

chain.name: Reconciliation
chain.plain: The license check. It compares what is installed and assigned with what was bought.

chain.name: Reclamation
chain.plain: Taking back licenses that nobody uses, so they can be reused instead of bought again.

outcomes.name: Compliant
outcomes.plain: We own at least what we use. Nothing to do.

outcomes.name: Under-licensed
outcomes.plain: We use more than we own. An audit could cost money.

outcomes.name: Over-licensed
outcomes.plain: We own more than we use. Money is tied up in unused licenses.

moves.intro: Six moves cover almost everything this guide asks you to do in ServiceNow. Learn them once in step 1.2; come back here whenever a step feels unclear.

moves.title: 1. Find a page with the All menu
how: Click **All** at the top left.
Type a few letters in the filter box, for example **update sets**.
Click the matching item in the results.
moves.tip: Type a list name such as **cmdb_ci_computer.list** and press Enter to open that list directly.

moves.title: 2. Open a page from this guide
how: Click a green **Open** button in a step. It opens the exact list or form in a new tab, already filtered to Northstar records.
The buttons need the instance address from step 0.5. Without it they show a name to copy into the All menu instead.
moves.tip: Leave the guide open in one browser tab and the instance in another.

moves.title: 3. Read a list
how: One row is one record.
The count is at the bottom right, for example **1 to 20 of 248**: 248 rows in total.
Click a column heading to sort by it.
moves.tip: A column you need is missing: right-click a column heading, choose **Configure**, **List Layout**, move the field to the right side and click **Save**.

moves.title: 4. Filter or group a list
how: Filter: click the funnel icon at the top left of the list. Choose a field, a condition and a value, and click **Run**.
Group: right-click a column heading and choose **Group By**.
Undo both: click **All** in the grey line above the list.
moves.tip: The grey line above the list always shows which filter is active.

moves.title: 5. Open and fill in a record
how: Click the blue text in the first column to open a record. Its form opens.
A red star marks a required field.
A field with a magnifier icon points to another record: type the first letters and pick from the list that appears.
A small **(i)** button next to such a field shows that record; click **Open Record** to go there.
Tabs below the fields (such as **General** or **Financial**) and lists at the bottom (such as **Roles**) hold more fields and linked records.
moves.tip: Grey fields cannot be changed. The system fills them in.

moves.title: 6. Save, or leave without saving
how: New record: **Submit** saves it and goes back to the list.
Existing record: **Update** saves it and goes back.
Save and stay on the form: right-click the grey header bar of the form and choose **Save**.
Leave without saving: click the back arrow at the top left of the form.
moves.tip: In the Software Asset Workspace the buttons are simply called **Save**, and **Publish** for entitlements.

extras.title: Scripts - Background
extras.text: A page where an admin pastes a script and clicks **Run script**. This guide uses it for 5 scripts. Each script says at the top what it does, and none of them deletes anything.

extras.title: Elevate role
extras.text: Some pages need a temporary extra permission. Click your picture (top right), **Elevate role**, tick **security_admin** and click **Update**. It lasts until you sign out.

extras.title: Execute Now
extras.text: Scheduled jobs normally run at night or once a week. Open the job and click **Execute Now** to start it at once. It runs in the background; check its result in the list the step names.

extras.title: Update sets
extras.text: The globe icon in the top bar shows which update set records your changes. Each stage starts its own.

glossary.plain: Assigning a license to a specific person or computer.
A short label that identifies one record. Our five purchases are tagged NSM-ENT-A to NSM-ENT-E, so scripts, reports and backups can find them.
A page (Scripts - Background) where an admin pastes a script and runs it once.
The final document that tells the project story to managers and interviewers.
ServiceNow's catalogue of known software products, used to recognise and clean names.
An online service that keeps the content library current on paid instances. A PDI does not have it.
Sample records ServiceNow can add when you switch on a product.
developer.servicenow.com, the website where you get and manage your PDI and switch on paid products for it.
The rule that connects found installations to a software model. On the model it shows as the tab Matching Discovery Models. A model without a match counts nothing.
One record for each unique combination of publisher, program name and version found on computers.
Switching on an extra admin permission, security_admin, for the current session. Some pages, such as Scripts - Background, need it.
A record of what was bought: product, how many, license metric, price and dates.
Screenshots that prove a result. They go in the repository's evidence folder.
ServiceNow's standard way to load a spreadsheet into a table, using a transform map.
A record saying that a program is installed on a computer. Also called a software installation or install.
One company's own copy of ServiceNow, reached at its own web address.
What you count to know how many licenses you need: per user, per device or per processor core.
The result of the license check for one product: compliant, under-licensed or over-licensed.
Cleaning messy software names into one standard name, for example turning 'Microsoft Visio Professional 2021 x64' into Microsoft Visio 2021 Professional.
How well a discovery model was cleaned: Normalized, Partially Normalized, Publisher Normalized, Match Not Found, Manually Normalized or New. Normalized and Manually Normalized count as clean.
Our invented company with 60 employees, 45 laptops and 12 servers.
Personal Developer Instance. A free ServiceNow instance for learning. It is our sandbox.
Paying for each processor core of a server. Microsoft sets minimums per processor and per server.
A package of features that you switch on in an instance. SAM Professional is a set of plugins.
Says whether software needs a license. Only software with product type Licensable is counted in the license check.
The button that switches on an entitlement. It changes the State from Build to In use; the license check ignores entitlements in Build.
Extra licensing rules for one vendor, such as Microsoft or Oracle, included in SAM Professional.
Taking back licenses that are not used so they can be reused.
The condition that decides when installed software counts as unused, for example not used for three months.
The license check. It compares what is installed and allocated with what was bought.
A ServiceNow version. There are two a year: Zurich (2025), Australia (May 2026) and Brazil (late 2026).
The options to fix a license problem, such as buying more licenses or removing installations.
An installation the system suggests removing because the reclamation rule found it unused.
A set of permissions given to a user, such as sam_admin or sam_user.
Software Asset Management: knowing what software you have and what you may use, and keeping the two in balance at the lowest cost.
ServiceNow's paid SAM product. It cleans software names, calculates license positions and knows the rules of big vendors.
A task the system runs automatically at set times. You can also start one at once with Execute Now.
A cloud platform many companies use to run IT and business processes, such as requests, incidents and assets, in one system.
A platform role that stops a user from creating, changing or deleting anything.
The modern screen in ServiceNow where SAM work is done.
The product as we manage it for licensing, for example Microsoft Visio Professional. It collects the matching installations.
Records of when a program was last used and for how long, normally collected by an agent on each computer.
Invented data that looks realistic but describes no real person or company.
Paying the vendor for use above what you bought, often after an audit.
The price of one right: one user, one device or one processor core. ServiceNow multiplies it by the number of rights to show money.
A container that records configuration changes so they can be exported as a backup or moved to another instance.

stages.title: Get your ServiceNow sandbox
stages.goal: Get a free personal ServiceNow instance on the Zurich release. Everything else in this project is built inside it.
stages.why: A [[PDI]] is a free sandbox from ServiceNow. Nothing we do in it can touch company systems.
before: Choose the sandbox owner. Each developer account can have one instance, and the owner must sign in to the Developer Site at least once a week.
Have a password manager ready. The admin password goes there and nowhere else.

steps.title: Sign in to the ServiceNow Developer Site
steps.what: Gets you into the [[Developer Site]], the free ServiceNow website where the sandbox is requested and managed.
do: Click **Open the Developer Site** below. It opens developer.servicenow.com in a new tab.
Click **Sign In** at the top right.
Type your email address and click **Next**. Type your password and click **Sign In**.
No account yet: click **Sign Up** instead, fill in the form, open the email you receive and click its link. Then sign in.
steps.see: You are signed in. Your name or picture shows at the top right.
help: The site shows an error or says it is busy: wait a few minutes and reload. The site had outages in 2026.
You forgot your password: click **Forgot password** on the sign-in page and follow the email.

steps.title: Check whether you already have an instance
steps.what: Each account can have only one instance. This step checks whether you already have one, so you never delete it by accident.
do: Look at the Developer Site home page. An existing instance shows as a card with its name (like dev123456) and its release.
Not on the home page: click your picture (top right) and look for **Manage instance** or **My instance**.
You have a **Zurich** instance: go straight to step 0.5.
You have an instance on another release and nothing in it matters to you: choose **Release instance** in its menu. Releasing deletes everything in it. Then go to step 0.3.
You have no instance: go to step 0.3.
steps.see: You know whether you already have an instance, and on which release.

steps.title: Request a Zurich instance
steps.what: Asks ServiceNow for a free instance on Zurich, the release this guide is written for.
do: Click **Request Instance** at the top right of the Developer Site.
In the list of releases, click **Zurich**. Do not choose Australia (newer) or Brazil (newest, still in early access).
Click **Request**.
Stay on the page. Most requests finish within a few minutes, and a box then shows the instance details. Go to step 0.5.
If the site says you are on a waitlist, stay on it and do step 0.4 while you wait. ServiceNow sends an email when the instance is ready.
Write the release and today's date in the box below.
steps.see: A box with the instance address, the user name **admin** and a password, or a message that you are on the waitlist.
help: "We were unable to assign an instance to you": sign out, go back to the Developer Site home page, sign in and try again.
On a waitlist: stay on it. Leaving and joining again puts you at the end. Waits of several days were common in 2026.
Zurich is not in the list: read **Zurich is not offered** under Troubleshooting below.

record.label: Release requested, and on which date

steps.title: While you wait: learn and prepare
steps.what: Uses the waiting time to learn what SAM is and what we are going to build.
do: Click **Basics in 5 minutes** in the menu on the left and read it.
Read files 01 to 05 in the repository's docs folder.
Open **Northstar files** in the Toolbox and look at the invented company we will build.
Come back when the email says your instance is ready.
steps.see: You can explain the five stories in your own words.

steps.title: Save the instance details
steps.what: Keeps the sign-in details safe, and gives this guide the instance address so its **Open** buttons go straight to the right ServiceNow pages.
do: On the Developer Site, find the instance details: **Instance URL** (like https://dev123456.service-now.com), **Username** (admin) and **Password**.
The details box is gone: click your picture (top right) and choose **Manage instance password**. The label can differ slightly.
Save the address, the user name **admin** and the password in your password manager. Never type the password into this guide, a chat or the repository.
Copy the instance address and paste it into **Instance address** below.
Type the initials of the sandbox owner below.
steps.see: The hint under the address says which address the Open buttons use, and the buttons in later steps say **Open**.

steps.title: Sign in and check that it is Zurich
steps.what: Proves that the instance works and that it runs Zurich.
do: Click **Open stats page** below. The ServiceNow sign-in page opens.
Type **admin** as user name and the password from your password manager. Click **Log in**.
If ServiceNow asks you to choose a new password, do it and update your password manager.
The stats page shows many technical lines. Find the line **Build name**.
Type what it says into **Build name** below.
steps.see: **Build name: Zurich**
help: Another release: stop here. Release the instance and request Zurich (step 0.3), or follow **Zurich is not offered** under Troubleshooting.
The page says the instance is asleep: sign in to the Developer Site and wake it. Waking takes 3 to 5 minutes, at most 20.

steps.title: Set the weekly reminder
steps.what: Keeps the sandbox alive. The Developer Site deletes an instance when its owner has not signed in for 10 days.
do: Open the sandbox owner's calendar.
Create a meeting that repeats every week, for example every Monday at 09:00.
Paste the reminder text below as its title.

copy.label: Reminder text
copy.value: Sign in to developer.servicenow.com (keeps the SAM sandbox alive)

steps.note: Signing in to the Developer Site also wakes an instance that went to sleep.
steps.see: The weekly reminder is in the owner's calendar.

checks.text: You can sign in to the instance as admin.
The stats page shows Build name Zurich, or the release rule was applied and written in tracker/decisions.md.
The admin password is only in a password manager.

problems.fix: Join the Zurich waitlist once and wait up to 7 days. If no Zurich instance arrives, request Australia, write the decision in tracker/decisions.md and carry on. Never call an Australia instance Zurich.
Sign in to the Developer Site and use the wake button. It takes 3 to 5 minutes, at most 20.
Developer Site, your picture (top right), Manage instance password. The label can differ slightly.

problems.problem: Still on the waitlist after many days
problems.fix: Keep your place. ServiceNow support does not handle PDIs. Use the time for the reading in step 0.4.

stages.title: Switch on SAM Professional
stages.time: 2 to 3 hours (the installation runs by itself for 1 to 2 hours)
stages.goal: Install Software Asset Management Professional with its sample data, check every part, open the Software Asset Workspace and write down how things look before we add our data.
stages.why: [[SAM Professional]] is a paid product. On a sandbox it can be switched on for free from the Developer Site. Checking each part now saves hours later.
before: Stage 0 is finished: you can sign in to the Zurich instance.
The instance is awake: open it once before you start.

steps.title: Start the SAM Professional installation
steps.what: Switches on [[SAM Professional]] and its [[demo data]] in your instance. The Developer Site does the work; it runs by itself for 1 to 2 hours.
do: Click **Open the Developer Site** below and check that you are signed in.
Click your picture (top right) and choose **Activate Plugin**. On some versions it is on the **Manage instance** page.
In the search box, type **Software Asset Management Professional**.
Click **Activate** next to it and choose the option **with demo data**. Confirm.
Click **Start timer** below. Do not change anything in the instance while it installs. Looking around is fine.
Write each attempt and its time in the box below.
steps.see: A message that the activation has started. Later the Developer Site shows it as complete, and you usually receive an email.
help: It failed: try once more. Failed again: follow **Activation keeps failing** under Troubleshooting.
Only an option without demo data: use it. Our own data arrives in Stage 2.
Not in the list: search for **Software Asset** and write down what you see.

record.label: Activation attempts, times and any error text

steps.title: Learn the six moves in ServiceNow
steps.what: Teaches the six moves you make on almost every ServiceNow page: find a page, open one from this guide, read a list, filter or group it, open a record, and save or leave it. It takes about 10 minutes and only looks, so it is safe while the installation runs.
do: Open **Moving around ServiceNow** below. It explains the same six moves in a few lines. Keep it open next to the instance.
**Move 1, find a page.** In the instance click **All** (top left) and type **users**. Click **Users** in the results. The user list opens.
**Move 2, open a page from this guide.** Click the **Users** button below. The same list opens in a new tab. Close that tab again.
**Move 3, read a list.** Look at the bottom right of the list. It says something like **1 to 20 of 600**: 600 rows in total.

**Move 4, filter or group.** Right-click the column heading **Department** and choose **Group By Department**. Click **All** in the grey line above the list to undo it. Then click the funnel icon at the top left, choose **First name**, keep **is**, type **Abel** and click **Run**. One row remains: Abel Tuter.
**Move 5, open a record.** Click **Abel Tuter**. The user form opens. Look at the fields, then scroll down to the tabs at the bottom, such as **Roles**.
**Move 6, save or leave.** Do not save anything now. Click the back arrow at the top left of the form to leave without saving.
steps.note: Saving works in two ways: **Submit** saves a new record and **Update** saves a changed one; both take you back to the list. Moving around ServiceNow also explains how to save and stay on the form.
steps.see: You can find a page, read a count, group, filter, open a record and leave it without saving.
help: No Abel Tuter: the demo users are missing. Try any other first name from the list.

steps.title: While it installs: read the basics
steps.what: Uses the waiting time to learn the words the next stages use.
do: Click **Basics in 5 minutes** in the menu on the left and read it.
Open **Northstar files** in the Toolbox and look at the people, computers and software we load in Stage 2.
steps.see: You can explain installation, entitlement and reconciliation in one sentence each.

steps.title: Start the change log for this stage
steps.what: Creates an [[update set]] for this stage. It records every setting we change, so Stage 6 can export it as a backup.
do: Click **Update sets** below. The list **Local Update Sets** opens.
Click **New** at the top of the list. An empty update set form opens.
Fill in **Name** as shown in the table.
Click **Submit and Make Current**.
steps.see: The list shows **SAM Portfolio S1 Foundation** with State **In progress**, and the globe icon in the top bar shows it as your current update set.
help: There is only a **Submit** button: click it, click the new update set in the list, then click **Make This My Current Set**.

To check the current update set at any time, click the globe icon in the top bar. No globe icon: click your picture (top right), **Preferences**, **Developer**, and switch on **Show update set picker in header**.
steps.note: Every stage from now on starts with its own update set. The data we load with scripts is not in update sets; the scripts in this guide can load it again at any time.

steps.title: Check the installed parts
steps.what: Confirms that the installation finished and records exactly which SAM parts and versions we have.
do: Wait until the Developer Site says the activation is complete. Then sign in to the instance again.
Click **Plugin list** below. It lists the [[plugin|plugins]] whose ID contains samp.
Check that they show as active.
Copy the **ID** and **Version** of each row into the box below, one per line.
steps.see: Several active plugins, for example **com.snc.samp**.
help: The list is empty or not filtered: in the search box above the list, choose **ID**, type ***samp** and press Enter.

steps.title: Check the SAM tables
steps.what: Makes sure the six main SAM lists exist and open without errors, and records how many sample rows they hold.
do: Click each button below. Each opens one list in a new tab.
Each list must open without an error message.
For the first four lists, read the count at the bottom right (for example **1 to 20 of 1,240**) and type the total in the table.
steps.see: Every list opens. With demo data the first four show rows. The last two may be empty.
help: "Invalid table" on one of the first four: the installation is not finished or failed. Go back to step 1.1.

steps.title: Check the SAM roles and automatic jobs
steps.what: Confirms the SAM permissions exist and finds the automatic jobs we start by hand in later stages.
do: Click **Roles** below. Find **sam_user** and **sam_admin** in the list.
Click **Scheduled jobs** below. It lists the jobs whose name starts with SAM.
Find the jobs for normalization, reconciliation and reclamation candidates, and copy their names into the box below.
steps.note: A [[role]] is a set of permissions. A [[scheduled job]] is a task the system runs on its own; we start some of them at once with **Execute Now**.
steps.see: **sam_user** and **sam_admin** exist, and several jobs start with **SAM**, such as **SAM - Software License Reconciliation**.

steps.title: Open the Software Asset Workspace
steps.what: Opens the [[Software Asset Workspace]], the modern screen where most SAM work and all results are shown.
do: Click **All** (top left) and type **Software Asset Workspace**.
Click **Software Asset Workspace** in the results. The workspace opens on the page **Software asset overview**.
Look at the menu on the left. It has views such as **License usage** and **License operations**. Click each one once.
Write in the box below whether it opened directly.
steps.see: The Software Asset Workspace opens and shows **License usage** and **License operations** in its menu.
help: It is not in the All menu, or it opens an empty page: this is a known sandbox problem. Do step 1.9, then come back.

record.label: Opened directly, or which fix worked

steps.title: Only if the workspace is missing: install it
steps.what: Fixes a known sandbox problem: SAM Professional sometimes arrives without its workspace. Skip this step when step 1.8 worked.
do: Click **All** and type **All Available Applications**. Click **All** under it. The application manager opens.
In its search box type **Software Asset Management Guided Experiences**. Older name: **Software Asset Management Playbooks and Guided Setups**.
Click the result, click **Install** and confirm. It brings the workspace with it. Wait until it shows as installed, 10 to 30 minutes.
Not listed: search **Software Asset Workspace** instead and install it. If it already shows as installed, open it and click **Repair**.
Sign out, close the browser, sign in again and repeat step 1.8.
Still missing: copy the workspace installer script below, run it in **Scripts - Background**, wait 30 minutes and repeat step 1.8.
Still missing after two tries: work in the classic menus (All, Software Asset). Every step in this guide also names the classic way. Write the decision in tracker/decisions.md.
steps.see: The Software Asset Workspace opens, or the classic-menu decision is written in tracker/decisions.md.

record.label: What you tried and what worked

steps.title: Check for the Content Service
steps.what: Records that the paid [[Content Service]] is not part of a sandbox. Stage 3 shows how we clean software names without it.
do: Click **Content Service setup** below.
Write what you see in the box below.
steps.see: On a sandbox this usually shows an error or an empty page. That is expected. If it opens with settings, write that down.

steps.title: Take the before picture of normalization
steps.what: Counts how clean the sample software names are before we start. This is the starting point for the case study.
do: Click **Discovery models** below.
Right-click the column heading **Normalization status** and choose **Group By Normalization status**.
Copy each group name and its count into the box below.
steps.note: [[Normalization]] cleans messy software names into standard ones.
steps.see: Groups such as Normalized, Partially Normalized, Publisher Normalized and Match Not Found, each with a count.
help: No column **Normalization status**: right-click any column heading, choose **Configure**, **List Layout**, move **Normalization status** to the right side and click **Save**.

steps.title: Give each team member their own login
steps.what: Lets every team member sign in with their own user, so nobody shares the admin password.
do: Click **Users** below, then **New**.
Fill in the form as shown in the table and click **Submit**.
Open the new user again. In the **Roles** tab at the bottom, click **Edit...**.
In the left box find **admin**, select it, click the arrow pointing right, then click **Save**.
Click **Set Password**, click **Generate**, copy the password, click **Save Password**. Give it to the person privately; they change it at first login.

rows.note: their own name, for example anna.devries

steps.see: Each team member signs in with their own user.

checks.text: SAM plugins are active, and their IDs and versions are written down.
The installation, discovery model, software model and entitlement lists open.
sam_user and sam_admin exist, and the SAM job names are written down.
The Software Asset Workspace opens, or the classic-menu fallback is written in tracker/decisions.md.
The Content Service result and the before counts of normalization are recorded.

problems.fix: 1) Wait 30 minutes, then try again from the Developer Site. 2) In the instance open All, All Available Applications, All. Search Software Asset Management and install the basic application if it is offered, then try the Developer Site again. 3) Write the exact error text and time in step 1.1. This order fixed repeated failures for others in 2025 and 2026.
Do step 1.9. It covers the Guided Experiences application, Repair, the installer script and the classic-menu fallback.
The demo data did not load. That is fine: our own data arrives in Stage 2.
Make sure you are signed in as admin. For scripts: your picture (top right), Elevate role, tick security_admin, Update.

stages.title: Create our fake company, Northstar
stages.goal: Load [[Northstar Manufacturing]] into the sandbox: 60 employees, 45 laptops, 12 servers and 248 software installations. The five license stories are built on this data.
stages.why: In a real company this data comes from scanning tools on every computer. In the sandbox one script plays that tool and creates the same records a scan would. All of it is [[synthetic data]].
before: Stage 1 is finished: SAM Professional is active and the workspace opens (or the fallback is noted).

steps.title: Start the change log for this stage
steps.what: Creates an [[update set]] for this stage. It records every setting we change, so Stage 6 can export it as a backup.
do: Click **Update sets** below. The list **Local Update Sets** opens.
Click **New** at the top of the list. An empty update set form opens.
Fill in **Name** as shown in the table.
Click **Submit and Make Current**.
steps.see: The list shows **SAM Portfolio S2 Data** with State **In progress**, and the globe icon in the top bar shows it as your current update set.
help: There is only a **Submit** button: click it, click the new update set in the list, then click **Make This My Current Set**.

To check the current update set at any time, click the globe icon in the top bar. No globe icon: click your picture (top right), **Preferences**, **Developer**, and switch on **Show update set picker in header**.

steps.title: Open Scripts - Background
steps.what: Opens the page where an admin pastes a script and runs it once. We use it to load Northstar.
do: Click **Scripts - Background** below. Or: click **All**, type **Scripts - Background** and click it.

steps.title: Understand the per core rule
steps.what: Explains in plain numbers why Windows Server needs 112 core licenses and SQL Server 24. You will be asked about this in every demo.
do: **Windows Server Standard** is licensed per core. Every physical server needs at least 16 core licenses, and every processor at least 8. Licenses come in packs of 2.
Our 4 application servers have 16 cores each: 64. Our 3 SQL servers have only 8 cores each, but the minimum is 16 per server: 48. Together 112. We own 112: **compliant**.

**SQL Server Standard** is licensed per core with at least 4 per processor. 3 servers with 2 processors of 4 cores need 24. We own 16: **8 short**. 8 cores at EUR 1,972.50 (4 packs of 2 cores at EUR 3,945) make **EUR 15,780** to pay after an audit.
Compare this with the Microsoft view from step 5.2 and write down what the system shows.
steps.note: Without the Microsoft rules a tool counts raw cores: 88 for Windows Server. [[Per core licensing]] minimums are why the right answer is 112.
